decision: Reject 150MHz and 175MHz for the unchanged shared realtime pipeline at canonical 15MS/s. Both pass short numerical replay but fail the 64-block burst/stall workload with energy-cache misses. Keep the deployed-candidate clock policy unchanged at 200MHz.
receiver_build_in_parallel: 18c96bb93f0aea5f868fb8b4c15a2eb1bce7a873, shared-realtime-bridge-summary-v1, original 100/200MHz clocks and full paired 15MS/s profile; completed22:49:41 UTC, 100MHz passes but200MHz fails. See starlink-bridge-counter-summary-20260909.json.

method.rounding: Round half-period upward to simulator1ps resolution, so actual stimulus is slightly slower than the requested frequency.
method.source_and_sink: Original bursty 15MS/s source cadence and score stalls; numerical fixture and all RTL/coefficients remain unchanged. Only generated FFT stimulus clock changes.
method.generated_core: Original 200MHz-targeted C_ARCH1 realtime XFFT9.1 configuration and exact generic checks; not regenerated for a lower-throughput architecture.

policy_tests.scope: Strict bounded clock choices before output allocation, explicit realtime selection, conservative period rounding, unchanged generated core settings, exact frozen RTL and clock-only generated bench delta. Not timing or throughput proof.

capacity4096.limit: Requested 4096 blocks, failed at the identical cycle and required/available cache indexes as the 64-block case. Not a completed 4096-block test.

interpretation: The required energy index is older than the oldest retained cache entry at each failure. These are actual observable integrity failures, not a pass inferred from a process exit or small FIFO high-water.
Interval score rates are computed from completed-block counts and the unchanged 100MHz simulation clock, not a whole-run or hardware throughput certification.
Larger buffers alone do not resolve a sustained producer/consumer rate deficit; scheduling or arithmetic throughput would need improvement before using these lower clocks.
Do not extrapolate exact RF timing accuracy, native 60MS/s calibration, every-frame measurements, production-duration reliability or a physical timing pass from these tests.

Any future clock redesign must preserve the AD9361's actual 200MHz IDELAY reference, independently implement the new clock/reset domain, and pass original-scope throughput, CDC, board timing and full receiver hardware gates.
